title: Parrot: Efficient Serving of LLM-based Applications with Semantic Variable
technique: Semantic Variable abstraction exposes request dataflow and per-variable performance criteria (latency vs throughput) to the service; DAG-aware scheduling, objective deduction, prefix sharing, cross-request pipelining

optimized_metrics.evidence: the system should minimize the end-to-end time it takes to receive the final summary, rather than the latency of individual requests.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: Figure 11 presents the average end-to-end latency

optimized_metrics.evidence: the ideal scheduling strategy should maximize the throughput ... (using higher batch sizes) during the map stage and minimize ... request latency during the reduce stage.
setting that an LLM engine can keep its generation latency ... under 40 ms/s for latency-sensitive requests

headline_claim.text: Parrot can achieve up to an order-of-magnitude improvement for popular and practical use cases of LLM applications. [Intro: up to 11.7× speedup or 12× higher throughput compared with the state-of-the-art solutions]

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the system should minimize the end-to-end time it takes to receive the final summary, rather than the latency of individual requests.
metric_definitions.notes: Application-level E2E = time from submission of the whole workflow (e.g. map-reduce summary, multi-agent) to the final output; includes inter-request network/queue overheads, which Parrot removes by server-side dataflow. Evaluation reports 'Average E2E latency' of chain/map-reduce/multi-agent apps.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: The get operation supports annotation of performance criteria, showing the end-to-end performance requirement of an application, which can be end-to-end latency or throughput (extensible to more criteria like per-token latency when streaming, and time-to-first-token).
metric_definitions.notes: Per-Semantic-Variable criterion; throughput-preferred vs latency-sensitive; deduced backwards from final outputs; latency-sensitive requests go to engines with capacity-limited batches, throughput-preferred requests (e.g. Map tasks of a task group) to large-batch engines.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the latency per output token, i.e. TPOT (Time-per-output-token) for vLLM, with continuous batching enabled, experiences a notable uptick when the engine's workload using a batch capacity beyond 6144.
metric_definitions.notes: Used only to set the baseline engine capacity; latency target 'under 40 ms/s' [sic, per token] for latency-sensitive requests.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: normalized latency (measured as request latency per number of output tokens)
metric_definitions.notes: Used for chat requests in the mixed chat+map-reduce workload (Fig 19).

slo_spec: No percentile SLOs; per-engine capacity threshold derived from TPOT knee (40 ms per token, 6144 batched tokens) for latency-sensitive requests.
load_regime: application workload runs at varying chunk size/output length and number of concurrent apps; mixed chat+map-reduce; no request-rate sweep with SLOs
tradeoff_acknowledged: Request-level: per-request latency of individual requests may be sacrificed for application-level completion time ('The latency of individual requests can sacrificed so as to reduce the completion time of the entire DAG'); throughput-oriented batching raises per-request latency (§3: 8.2x throughput for 95% higher latency).
hardware: Server with 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB; server with 4x NVIDIA A6000 48GB
workloads: Chain/Map-Reduce summarization, Bing Copilot trace, GPTs apps, MetaGPT multi-agent, mixed chat+map-reduce
extractor_notes: Key distinction made explicit: request-level latency (what existing services optimize) vs application end-to-end time (what Parrot optimizes) - PROGRAM_JCT is measured as average E2E latency of the application run, includes client-server network latency in the baseline. No tail percentiles. 'ms/s' unit in text for per-token target is a typo-like unit. Throughput appears both as objective for map tasks and as headline (12x).
load_class_quote: arrival time follows Poisson distri ... mix of requests from chat applications at a rate of 1 req/s [§8: ShareGPT/Bing Copilot request-rate sweeps (Poisson), but chain/map-reduce app latencies measured as app runs at varying chunk size/output length without arrival process]
